newsitem.title: DUBAI: Two Filipinos die in test of big oil tanker.
newsitem.headline: Two Filipinos die in test of big oil tanker.

text.p: Two Filipino crewmen died and four others were injured when their lifeboat crashed during a routine safety test of one of the world's largest oil tankers berthed in Dubai, a local newspaper said on Monday.

The incident occurred on November 25 while the Norwegian-flagged 564,763 dwt ultra large crude carrier (ULCC) Jahre Vicking was undergoing three weeks of general repairs at Dubai Dry Docks, the United Arab Emirates English-language Khaleej Times added.
The two seamen died instantly after their lifeboat, whose seaworthiness was being tested, crashed about 35 metres into the sea, it added.
The 1976-built tanker, which transports crude oil from Saudi Arabia to the United States, left Dubai on November 30.
Preliminary investigations have indicated that the tanker's lifeboat chain snapped at a point where it had been welded as it was being lowered in test trials, the newspaper said.
